name_en: Futago satoimo — sticky heirloom taro from the Kitakami River in Iwate
summary_ja: 岩手県北上市の二子町周辺で受け継がれてきたさといも。煮るととろけるようなねっとりした舌ざわりが持ち味とされ、北上川の川岸で鍋を囲む秋の芋煮会や、いもの子汁に欠かせない芋として親しまれているという。
summary_en: A taro handed down around Futago, a district of Kitakami in Iwate. Simmered, it turns meltingly soft and sticky, and it is the taro people reach for in imonoko-jiru, the autumn taro soup cooked in big pots on the banks of the Kitakami River.
source_title: いもの子汁 岩手県 | うちの郷土料理

name_en: Mikatahara bareisho — thin-skinned spring potatoes from Hamamatsu's red-earth plateau
summary_ja: 静岡県浜松市の三方原台地で育つじゃがいも。冬に植えて春から初夏に掘り上げる新じゃがが中心で、皮が薄く、身はきめ細かくしっとりして、ほのかな甘みがあるとされる。皮ごと煮たり揚げたりして味わうことが多いという。
summary_en: Potatoes grown on the Mikatahara plateau in Hamamatsu, Shizuoka. Planted in winter and dug from spring into early summer, they reach market mostly as new potatoes — thin-skinned, fine-textured, moist and faintly sweet — and are often cooked whole with the skin on.

name_en: Tanba yama-no-imo — knobbly, intensely sticky mountain yam from the Sasayama basin
summary_ja: 兵庫県丹波篠山市を中心に育つ、黒っぽい皮でごつごつと丸い山の芋。すりおろすと器を傾けても流れにくいほど粘りが強いとされ、とろろや、皮に芋を練り込む薯蕷饅頭などの和菓子に使われてきたという。
summary_en: A round, knobbly, dark-skinned mountain yam grown mainly around Tanba-Sasayama in Hyogo. Grated, it is said to be so sticky it barely moves when the bowl is tilted, and it has long gone into tororo and into wagashi such as joyo manju, whose dough is made with grated yam.
source_title: 丹波篠山市公式サイト

name_en: Okinawa beni-imo — purple-fleshed sweet potato of the Ryukyu islands
summary_ja: 皮も身も赤紫から濃い紫色をした沖縄のさつまいも。読谷村などで栽培され、あざやかな色が餡や菓子に生かされている。生のいもは害虫の広がりを防ぐ制度で県外へ持ち出せないため、多くはペーストや粉に加工されて県外へ渡るという。
summary_en: Okinawa's sweet potato with skin and flesh ranging from reddish to deep purple. Grown in Yomitan and elsewhere, its vivid color is put to work in sweet pastes and confectionery. Because fresh tubers may not leave the prefecture under pest-control rules, most of what reaches the rest of Japan travels as paste or powder.

name_en: Tanba dainagon azuki — large red beans from Tanba that keep their shape when simmered
summary_ja: 兵庫県と京都府にまたがる丹波地方で育つ、大粒で色の濃い小豆。煮ても皮が破れにくく、粒の形を保ったままふっくら炊き上がるとされ、粒あんや甘納豆、鹿の子といった粒を見せる和菓子に重んじられてきたという。
summary_en: Large, deep-red azuki beans grown in the Tanba region, which straddles Hyogo and Kyoto. They are said to keep their skins intact and their shape whole when simmered, which is why confectioners have long favored them for wagashi that show off the whole bean, such as tsubu-an, amanatto and kanoko.

name_en: Ibusuki sora-mame — early-season broad beans from Kagoshima's warm southern tip
summary_ja: 鹿児島県指宿市を中心に、冬から春にかけて出荷されるそらまめ。霜のほとんど降りない薩摩半島の南端で育ち、本州の産地より早く出回るとされる。大粒でほっくりとした豆を、塩ゆでや莢ごとの焼きで味わうという。
summary_en: Broad beans grown mainly around Ibusuki in Kagoshima and shipped from winter into spring. Raised at the nearly frost-free southern tip of the Satsuma Peninsula, they reach market ahead of crops from Honshu. The large, floury beans are eaten boiled in salted water or roasted in the pod.
